governanceNotes: D1 batch 79 (2026-09-27): two bounded association edges authored - riedel-s-thyroiditis to hypothyroidism (rank 1) and riedel-s-thyroiditis to hypoparathyroidism (rank 2) - both classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory SYSTEMIC_INFLAMMATORY on both, reflecting that one IgG4-related fibrosing process supplies both the parenchymal destruction and the adjacent-gland involvement. The edges rest on disjoint sources this batch (deliberately no within-batch shared-source provenance while the CRG redundancy-semantics question stands at eleven accumulated examples): the hypothyroidism edge on the 2018 Karolinska series of six patients (hypothyroidism at diagnosis in five, extrathyroidal manifestations in four, IgG4/IgG ratio over 40 percent in one, PMID 29380231), the 2011 clinical review (biochemical constellation of hypocalcaemia and hypothyroidism with restrictive symptoms out of proportion to mass, PMID 21832114), and the 2016 IgG4-related thyroid-disorder review (levothyroxine for resulting hypothyroidism as a primary treatment option, PMID 27828690); the hypoparathyroidism edge on the 2015 case report documenting silently present hypocalcaemia with inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone and return to the reference range within three months of isthmectomy plus corticosteroids and tamoxifen, together with the one-seventh frequency statement (PMID 26200816), the 2023 case report independently reproducing that reversibility (PMID 36937637), and the 2022 six-patient surgical series reporting temporary postoperative hypoparathyroidism alongside vocal-cord palsy (PMID 36452560). Route-separation discipline: the two hypoparathyroidism mechanisms - intrinsic parathyroid infiltration by the fibrotic process and postoperative deficiency after fibrotic dissection - are carried explicitly and separately rather than blended, and the frequency figure is attributed to its single-case-report origin. Window discipline: the hypothyroidism edge is deliberately kept distinct from the registered rel-thyroiditis-to-hypothyroidism edge, which scopes itself to chronic autoimmune or Hashimoto-type disease, by naming coexisting autoimmune thyroiditis as the principal competing explanation in the causation status, evidence gaps, and alternatives. Constitutive-proximity applied to withhold dysphagia, the presenting symptom in essentially every anchor. The nontoxic-thyroid-enlargement, thyroid-cancer, vocal-cord-paralysis, tracheal-stenosis, and extrathyroidal-involvement propositions are withheld on the record with reasons, the last three as catalog-gap continuations.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Riedel's thyroiditis is an IgG4-related fibroinflammatory process that destroys the thyroid gland and is accompanied by hypothyroidism across clinical series and reviews: the 2018 Karolinska series of six patients with Riedel's thyroiditis reports that five of the six had hypothyroidism at diagnosis, that extrathyroidal manifestations were present in four, and that one patient had a clear IgG4/IgG ratio over 40 percent, with four treated with glucocorticoids, four with tamoxifen, and two with both (PMID 29380231); the 2011 clinical review states that Riedel's presentation includes characteristic biochemical abnormalities such as hypocalcaemia and hypothyroidism, that local restrictive or infiltrative symptoms out of proportion to a demonstrable mass or simultaneous biochemical abnormalities are a diagnostic clue, and that the condition is commonly treated with long-term anti-inflammatory medication to arrest progression (PMID 21832114); and the 2016 review of IgG4-related thyroid disorders states that levothyroxine supplementation for the resulting hypothyroidism remains one of the primary treatment options alongside glucocorticoids, appropriate management of Graves' disease, and surgical excision where compressive symptoms require it (PMID 27828690); recorded as documented association only with the anchor-class limits carried openly - the only located clinical series has six patients of whom five were hypothyroid, the review anchor describes the association without quantifying it, and the third anchor is a review of the wider IgG4-related thyroid disease group in which Riedel's thyroiditis is one member rather than an isolated population.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of hypothyroidism is established for any individual: the located clinical series is six patients of whom five were hypothyroid at diagnosis with no euthyroid comparator and no denominator, both reviews describe the association at framework level, the condition shares a thyroid-gland window with chronic autoimmune thyroiditis whose own registered edge to hypothyroidism is explicitly bounded to autoimmune Hashimoto-type disease, and exogenous levothyroxine administration in the located cases means thyroid-function values in treated individuals cannot be read as untreated natural history; individual claims require dated thyroid-function studies demonstrating hypothyroidism, dated Riedel's diagnosis with histological or IgG4 confirmation, and exclusion of chronic autoimmune thyroiditis, Hashimoto's disease, prior thyroid radioiodine or surgery, iodine exposure, and pituitary disease.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: IgG4-mediated lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with storiform fibrosis progressively replaces and destroys thyroid parenchyma - the fibroinflammatory process the series anchors describe - so that hormone synthesis falls and hypothyroidism follows, but whether the fibrotic destruction produced any individual's hypothyroidism rather than a coexisting autoimmune thyroiditis remains hypothesized until the thyroid function, the histology, and the antibody profile are read together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at clinical-series, clinical-review, and disease-group-review class following the thyroiditis-to-hypothyroidism convention (the registered rel-thyroiditis-to-hypothyroidism edge, which scopes itself to chronic autoimmune or Hashimoto-type thyroiditis and explicitly not every transient or destructive thyroiditis syndrome, and the registered rel-postpartum-thyroiditis-to-hypothyroidism edge): the clinical-series anchor is the only located cohort with patient-level thyroid-function data and reports hypothyroidism in five of six patients at diagnosis alongside extrathyroidal manifestations in four (PMID 29380231), the clinical-review anchor supplies the biochemical constellation and the diagnostic weighting of restrictive symptoms out of proportion to mass (PMID 21832114), and the IgG4 thyroid-disorder review supplies the treatment-framing anchor in which levothyroxine for the resulting hypothyroidism is a primary option (PMID 27828690); because the located cohort is six patients without a euthyroid comparator and both reviews are descriptive, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with the anchor class stated and the autoimmune-thyroiditis alternative named, so the edge does not collapse into the registered autoimmune-thyroiditis window.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The only located clinical series is six patients with five hypothyroid at diagnosis, with no euthyroid comparator, no denominator, and no reported confidence interval, so the frequency of hypothyroidism in the condition cannot be estimated; both review anchors describe the association at framework level and the third anchor addresses the wider IgG4-related thyroid disease group in which Riedel's thyroiditis is one member, so its figures are not specific to this condition; several located patients were treated with levothyroxine, so their thyroid-function values reflect treatment rather than untreated natural history; no located anchor separates Riedel's thyroiditis from a coexisting autoimmune thyroiditis by antibody profile, which is the principal competing explanation for the thyroid failure.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Coexisting chronic autoimmune or Hashimoto's thyroiditis, the principal competing explanation for the thyroid failure and the subject of the registered bounded thyroiditis-to-hypothyroidism edge
Prior thyroid surgery, radioiodine treatment, or therapeutic irradiation damaging the gland
Iodine exposure, amiodarone, lithium, or antithyroid medication affecting thyroid function
Central hypothyroidism from pituitary or hypothalamic disease, which the reviews do not separate

evidenceGaps: The only located clinical series is six patients with five hypothyroid at diagnosis, with no euthyroid comparator, no denominator, and no reported confidence interval, so the frequency of hypothyroidism in the condition cannot be estimated; both review anchors describe the association at framework level and the third anchor addresses the wider IgG4-related thyroid disease group in which Riedel's thyroiditis is one member, so its figures are not specific to this condition; several located patients were treated with levothyroxine, so their thyroid-function values reflect treatment rather than untreated natural history; no located anchor separates Riedel's thyroiditis from a coexisting autoimmune thyroiditis by antibody profile, which is the principal competing explanation for the thyroid failure.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because the gland destruction and the biochemical failure are documented together in a patient-level series and in two reviews, and because the mechanism names the fibrosing inflammation rather than a generic thyroid failure; the conservative framing states the six-patient anchor, the lack of a euthyroid comparator, the exogenous levothyroxine in the located cases, and the coexisting-autoimmune-immune alternative, so the edge remains distinct from the registered autoimmune thyroiditis window.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Riedel's thyroiditis is repeatedly documented to involve the parathyroid glands, producing hypocalcaemia with an inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone level, and the deficit is reported to be reversible when the fibrotic process is treated: the 2015 report describes a 40-year-old woman with progressive thyroid enlargement, worsening dysphagia, and positional dyspnoea with a hard non-mobile goiter, whose marked asymptomatic hypocalcaemia with an inappropriately normal parathyroid hormone level was treated with isthmectomy followed by serial corticosteroid and tamoxifen, after which serum calcium and parathyroid hormone returned to the reference range within three months, and which states that about one-seventh of Riedel's thyroiditis cases are associated with hypoparathyroidism necessitating long-term therapy for symptomatic hypocalcaemia while in most cases the deficit persists and requires continued treatment (PMID 26200816); the 2023 case report describes a patient treated with levothyroxine, calcium, and alfacalcidol in whom total thyroidectomy was not performed because of hard adhesion to neighbouring structures, whose biopsy was consistent with Riedel's thyroiditis and who was treated with glucocorticoids with resolution of compressive symptoms, decrease in thyroid volume, and normalisation of serum calcium and parathyroid hormone after discontinuation of vitaminocalcic supplementation, noting that hypoparathyroidism may be clinically asymptomatic (PMID 36937637); and the 2022 series of six Riedel's thyroiditis cases in which five underwent surgical management (four total thyroidectomies, one hemithyloidy) reports postoperative complications of temporary hypoparathyroidism, unilateral vocal cord palsy, and temporary bilateral vocal cord palsy, with the fibrotic process stabilised or resolved in all patients (PMID 36452560); recorded as documented association only with the anchor-class and direction limits carried openly - the condition is rare and the located evidence is one case with a quantified frequency statement, one case, and a six-patient surgical series, and the surgical anchor's hypoparathyroidism is postoperative while the other two describe parathyroid involvement by the fibrotic process itself, so the fibrotic-infiltration and the surgical routes are distinct and both are carried.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of hypoparathyroidism is established for any individual: the located evidence is two case reports and one six-patient surgical series, the quantified frequency statement of about one-seventh comes from a single case report's literature summary rather than a cohort, the postoperative hypoparathyroidism in the surgical series is a treatment-mediated route through thyroidectomy that must be separated from intrinsic parathyroid involvement by the fibrotic process, and the deficit was clinically silent in the strongest anchor so it is found by bioassay rather than by symptoms; individual claims require dated parathyroid hormone, calcium, and phosphate values showing an inappropriately normal or low hormone level in the presence of hypocalcaemia, dated Riedel's diagnosis with histological or IgG4 confirmation, and separation of intrinsic parathyroid involvement from postoperative deficiency after any thyroid or parathyroid surgery.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Fibrosing infiltration of the parathyroid glands by the same IgG4-related process that replaces thyroid parenchyma - the mechanism the case anchors describe when hypoparathyroidism resolves alongside resolution of the fibrotic process on glucocorticoids - reduces parathyroid hormone output and produces hypocalcaemia, while in the surgical population inadvertent parathyroid devascularisation or removal during difficult fibrotic dissection supplies a second route; whether either route produced any individual's hypoparathyroidism remains hypothesized until the parathyroid biochemistry and the surgical history are read together.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report, case-report, and surgical-series class following the post-thyroid-surgery convention (the registered rel-nontoxic-thyroid-enlargement-to-hypoparathyroidism and rel-thyroid-cancer-to-hypoparathyroidism edges, both of which own their own surgical routes with sources left untouched per ME-29): the 2015 anchor is the strongest located evidence because it documents the deficit silently present at baseline, the quantified frequency statement of about one-seventh, and the return of parathyroid hormone to the reference range within three months of treating the fibrotic process (PMID 26200816), the 2023 anchor independently reproduces that reversibility and documents asymptomatic presentation (PMID 36937637), and the surgical anchor supplies the treatment-mediated route with its own postoperative complication profile (PMID 36452560); because the intrinsic and surgical routes are distinct mechanisms, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, carries both routes explicitly rather than blending them, and routes individual claims through parathyroid biochemistry that can separate them.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are small (two case reports and a six-patient series) and the one-seventh frequency statement originates in a single case report's literature summary rather than in a cohort denominator; the two case anchors describe intrinsic parathyroid involvement by the fibrotic process while the surgical anchor describes postoperative deficiency, so no anchor combines both routes in one population; the strongest anchor's hypoparathyroidism was clinically silent and detected on bioassay, so its presence depends on routine parathyroid testing that is not universally performed; the surgical anchor reports only temporary hypoparathyroidism in a series where five of six patients underwent surgery, so it cannot establish how often the deficit follows conservative management.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Postoperative hypoparathyroidism after thyroidectomy or parathyroid surgery, the treatment-mediated route the surgical anchor reports and the necessary comparator to the intrinsic route
Postoperative hypocalcaemia from hungry-bone syndrome or transient ischaemic parathyroid injury without anatomic removal
Coexisting autoimmune polyglandular syndrome or magnesium-related functional hypoparathyroidism
Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder producing a different parathyroid axis abnormality

evidenceGaps: All three anchors are small (two case reports and a six-patient series) and the one-seventh frequency statement originates in a single case report's literature summary rather than in a cohort denominator; the two case anchors describe intrinsic parathyroid involvement by the fibrotic process while the surgical anchor describes postoperative deficiency, so no anchor combines both routes in one population; the strongest anchor's hypoparathyroidism was clinically silent and detected on bioassay, so its presence depends on routine parathyroid testing that is not universally performed; the surgical anchor reports only temporary hypoparathyroidism in a series where five of six patients underwent surgery, so it cannot establish how often the deficit follows conservative management.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because two independent case anchors document the deficit, its silent presentation, and its reversal when the fibrotic process is treated - which is strong mechanistic detail despite small samples - and a surgical series supplies the second route with a complication profile; the conservative framing keeps the intrinsic and surgical routes separate, attributes the frequency figure to its single-case-report origin, and requires parathyroid biochemistry capable of separating the two, so a reader cannot infer that thyroidectomy or fibrotic infiltration caused a given individual's deficit without distinguishing them.
